item.title: The good life ★★★
item.description: It turned out that this was actually two books in one - “Living the good life,” from 1954, and “Continuing the good life,” from 1979. The first reads as genuinely groundbreaking, a prefacing of the back-to-the-land and hippie movements of the 60s but starting thirty years earlier; the second a more tired rehashing of the first with some complaints about all the rich kid hippies taking any soul-searching. Although they have some annoyingly self-righteous habits, our life does kind of line up with their precepts (except that we don’t live on a farm and shop at grocery stores).

item.title: Martyr! ★★★
item.description: A strange novel, unlike most other things I’ve read but maybe most similar to Infinite Jest and A Little Life; I liked those better than this. About Iran, AA and recovery, creating a world with your friends.

item.title: History of the world in bite-sized chunks ★★
item.description: A pretty good summary of “the history of civilization” that seems to want credit for including African and American history. Eventually I realized it was British and its view of history suddenly made sense (e.g., Charles Martel “saving” Europe from Islam, mentioning Scottish explorers of Africa, &c.).

item.title: Admiral Hornblower in the West Indies ★★★
item.description: A series of largely disconnected stories of Hornblower’s escapades in, yes, the West Indies. Overall, my review of the hornblower series is that they are marvelously fun, pretty historically and logistically accurate, and 100% British propaganda.
